days.title: Highland Peaks and Lava Deserts
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Kverkfjöll
stops.detail: In the cut (Icelandic: kverk) between these two glaciers rises the mountain massif of Kverkfjöll.

stops.name: Herðubreið
stops.detail: After both rivers flow more or less parallel to each other for 40 km, it flows into the Jökulsá á Fjöllum below the Herðubreið, which had flowed northeast until then.

stops.name: Ódáðahraun
stops.detail: From then on, the river becomes wider and flows through the Ódáðahraun, a largely desert-like area characterized by eroded lava and ash fields.

days.title: Waterfalls of the Jökulsárgljúfur Canyon
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Selfoss
stops.detail: In the last approx. 50 km, the river, which has become a stream, pours successively over three large waterfalls, the Selfoss, the Dettifoss and the Hafragilsfoss, to finally enter the lowlands through a deep three-part gorge Jökulsárgljúfur created by itself.

stops.name: Dettifoss
stops.detail: Its average water volume at the Dettifoss waterfall is 183 m³/s.

stops.name: Hafragilsfoss
stops.detail: At the Hafragilsfoss waterfall and in Vesturdalur (a valley in today's Jökulsárgljúfur National Park), volcanic eruptions from fissures directly under the river, which belong to the Askja volcanic system, also shaped the landscape in enormous hydromagmatic explosions about 6,000 years ago.

days.title: Canyons and Valleys of the North
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Jökulsárgljúfur
stops.detail: Here it flows over the waterfalls Selfoss, Hafragilsfoss and Dettifoss and through the gorge Jökulsárgljúfur in the national park of the same name.

stops.name: Ásbyrgi
stops.detail: From the level of Ásbyrgi, the river flows for about 20 km north in several arms, finally flowing into the Greenland Sea in the Kelduhverfi in the bay of Öxarfjörður.
